issues.legal_issue: A landlord may establish a bona fide need for demolition and reconstruction without relying on the building’s age or condition as the decisive basis for eviction.
material_facts: The premises included an old building and a substantially larger area of open land; the evidence also supported a finding that the building was dilapidated and needed reconstruction.
The landlords proposed to demolish the building and construct a multi-storey complex, and plans for the proposed construction had been prepared.
The landlords had the financial means to undertake reconstruction and explained how they would arrange the necessary funds.
The property was underutilized, multi-storey buildings had been constructed nearby, and the proposed development would make more useful space available.
The appellate authority denied eviction because the landlords had said they were not relying on the building’s condition; the High Court restored the eviction order.
issues.conclusion: The landlords’ bona fide need for demolition and reconstruction was established, and the High Court was right to restore eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1)(b) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Control) Act, 1960, the building’s age and condition are relevant but not determinative of the landlord’s bona fides. The court assesses the genuine intention to reconstruct, the building’s age and condition, the landlord’s financial capacity, the useful utilization of the property, and the genuine desire for economic advantage. Vijay Singh v. Vijayalakshmi Ammal held that age and condition are not the sole determinative factors; R.V.E. Venkatachala Gounder v. Venkatesha Gupta recognized the relevance of capacity, useful utilization, and economic advantage. The earlier approach in P. Orr and Sons (P) Ltd. v. Associated Publishers (Madras) Ltd., which treated condition as determinative of urgency and bona fides, was displaced by the Constitution Bench decision in Vijay Singh.

rule.if: demolition_eviction_proceeding and landlord_genuine_reconstruction_intent and landlord_financial_capacity and (building_old_or_dilapidated or property_underutilized or redevelopment_has_useful_economic_purpose)

predicates.demolition_eviction_proceeding: The case is a proceeding seeking eviction so that the landlord can demolish and reconstruct the premises.
predicates.landlord_genuine_reconstruction_intent: The landlord proposed reconstruction for a genuine purpose beyond merely getting rid of the tenant.
predicates.landlord_financial_capacity: The landlord had the means, or a credible means of arranging funds, to carry out the proposed reconstruction.
predicates.building_old_or_dilapidated: The building was old or in a condition that supported reconstruction.
predicates.property_underutilized: The premises included substantial space that was open or otherwise not put to effective use.
predicates.redevelopment_has_useful_economic_purpos: The proposed redevelopment was expected to make the property more useful or provide a genuine economic advantage.

issues.definition: When a demolition-eviction proceeding involves a genuine reconstruction plan, financial capacity, and at least one relevant circumstance concerning the building or the useful purpose of redevelopment, the landlord qualifies for eviction on the demolition ground.

issues.legal_issue: The operation of a private, unrecognized school in the premises does not by itself bar eviction for bona fide demolition and reconstruction when redevelopment would provide broader useful accommodation.
material_facts: The tenant operated an unrecognized private school in the premises, serving children of non-resident Indians and earning income from its operation.
The proposed reconstruction would make the property more fully useful and could provide housing and, in part, space for business or commerce.
issues.conclusion: Eviction was not to be denied in the name of public interest merely because the tenant operated a school in the premises.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1)(b) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Control) Act, 1960 permits eviction on the demolition-and-reconstruction ground when its requirements are met. The court found no basis to treat the private operation of an unrecognized school as a public-interest reason to defeat that ground where reconstruction could provide shelter and other useful space.

predicates.demolition_eviction_proceeding: The case is a proceeding seeking eviction so that the landlord can demolish and reconstruct the premises.
predicates.tenant_operates_private_unrecognized_sch: The tenant operated a private school in the premises that was not recognized.
predicates.redevelopment_would_provide_broader_usef: The proposed reconstruction could provide housing or other useful accommodation beyond the existing use.

issues.definition: In a demolition-eviction proceeding, operation of a private unrecognized school does not bar eviction when redevelopment would provide broader useful accommodation.

issues.legal_issue: An eviction decree for reconstruction may be made executable only after the required construction plans are approved and the landlord provides the required undertaking, with protection for the tenant pending execution.
material_facts: Local approval of construction plans was required before reconstruction could proceed.
The landlords had prepared plans but had not yet submitted them to the local authority for approval.
The tenant apprehended that the premises might be vacated and demolished without reconstruction proceeding if approval was not obtained.

The court directed the landlords to submit the plans, required approved plans to be produced before the Executing Court, and required an undertaking there; it also directed that the tenant receive reasonable time to vacate and continue paying use-and-occupation charges until then.
issues.conclusion: The eviction decree was maintained but could be executed only after approved plans were produced and the required undertaking was filed; the tenant was to receive reasonable time to vacate and remain liable for use-and-occupation charges until then.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1)(b) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Control) Act, 1960, eviction may be ordered for demolition and reconstruction. Section 14(2)(b) requires the landlord’s undertaking. Where local approval is necessary and plans have not yet been sanctioned, execution may be conditioned on submission and approval of the plans and compliance with the undertaking requirement, thereby protecting both landlord and tenant.

rule.if: demolition_eviction_decree and local_approval_required and reconstruction_plans_not_yet_approved and landlord_has_prepared_reconstruction_plans

predicates.demolition_eviction_decree: The case involves an eviction decree granted to permit demolition and reconstruction.
predicates.local_approval_required: Local rules require approval of plans before the proposed reconstruction can be carried out.
predicates.reconstruction_plans_not_yet_approved: The plans for the proposed reconstruction had not received the necessary approval.
predicates.landlord_has_prepared_reconstruction_pla: The landlord had prepared plans for the proposed reconstruction.

issues.definition: When an eviction decree for reconstruction involves a requirement for local approval and the prepared plans are not yet approved, execution requires approved plans and the required undertaking.
